title: Accessible contact form with local validation
description: A labeled name, email, and message form using native required-field validation. This self-contained demo only checks input locally: it sends no request and claims no delivery. The submit button stays disabled until the explicit JavaScript listener is ready. Connect a real application submission flow before offering to send messages.
html:
Contact the garden team

Local demo: nothing you enter is sent or saved. All fields are required.

Use an address where you can receive replies.
checks: Run the JavaScript after this HTML exists; without JavaScript the submit button must remain disabled and no data should be submitted.
Use a keyboard to submit with missing fields and an invalid email; native validation must identify the field and preserve entered values.
Verify persistent labels, required indications, autocomplete, hint association, and status announcement with a screen reader.
Confirm that a valid submit makes no network request and reports only local validity, not successful delivery or a promised reply.
When integrating real submission, add server validation, privacy safeguards, and text errors connected with aria-describedby; test failure as well as success.

title: Native modal dialog with explicit open and close listeners
description: A named modal packing checklist opened with showModal() and closed with close() through explicit addEventListener calls, never inline handlers. Native dialog supplies modal behavior and Escape handling; test focus containment and restoration in the target browser. This is informational, not a simulated destructive action.
html:
Prepare for a garden visit

Review what to bring before you leave home.

Packing checklist

Bring these items for an outdoor visit.

  • A refillable water bottle
  • Closed-toe shoes
  • A hat and weather-appropriate clothing
checks: Open using the keyboard; confirm the dialog name and short description are announced and initial focus is on Close checklist.
Tab and Shift+Tab must not reach the background while the modal is open; test this in an actual browser, not just static lint.
Close with the explicit button and with Escape, then verify focus returns to View packing checklist in both cases.
Do not replace showModal() with an open attribute toggle or add redundant aria-modal and hand-written focus traps.
Check long content at high zoom, visible focus, dark theme, and the no-JavaScript or unsupported-browser guidance.

title: Native help popover with a details fallback
description: Non-modal help using native popovertarget and popover=auto, with a working details/summary disclosure as the no-JavaScript and unsupported-browser fallback. Feature detection swaps the fallback for the native controls. Prefer details alone when an in-flow disclosure is enough; do not use a popover as a modal dialog or hover-only tooltip.
html:
Watering guidance

Check the soil first

Feel the soil below the surface. If it is dry, water the soil slowly rather than wetting the leaves.

When should I water?

Feel the soil below the surface. If it is dry, water the soil slowly rather than wetting the leaves.
checks: Without JavaScript, and in a browser without popover support, only the details disclosure should be available; open it with Enter or Space.
In a supporting browser, verify the native panel starts closed after enhancement, opens with the trigger, and closes with its button, Escape, or light dismissal.
Verify keyboard access, native expanded-state announcement, reading order, and focus behavior with the target browser and screen reader; non-modal help must not trap focus.
Do not set display:block on a closed popover or leave the hidden attribute on the enhanced panel; either can defeat native visibility behavior.
Keep both copies of the help text synchronized. Prefer the simpler details-only version when floating content is unnecessary.

title: Responsive card grid with semantic articles
description: Three informational workshop cards use semantic articles and Sprig's auto-fit grid. The supported --sprig-column custom property sets the preferred column width without a framework or breakpoint script. Content is not a fake clickable card; add a real destination link only when there is somewhere to navigate.
html:
Choose a workshop format

Compare activities for a community garden session.

Beginner friendly

Seed starting

Practice filling pots, sowing seeds, and labeling what you planted.

Suggested session length: 45 minutes.

Hands-on

Compost basics

Sort sample materials and explore how moisture and air help a compost pile.

Suggested session length: 60 minutes.

Indoor option

Plan a small plot

Sketch a growing space and compare plants with different light needs.

Suggested session length: 30 minutes.
checks: Resize from a wide viewport to 320 CSS pixels and test 400% zoom; cards must reflow without page-level horizontal scrolling or clipped words.
Check heading levels in the host page; keep one section heading followed by article headings, adapting the levels when embedded.
Preserve DOM reading order instead of visually reordering cards with CSS.
Do not add tabindex, click handlers, or role=button to informational articles; use descriptive links for real navigation and buttons for actual actions.
Check badge contrast and card boundaries in both themes and forced-colors mode; do not rely on color to convey a category.

title: Wrapping navigation with a keyboard skip link
description: A page shell with a first-focusable skip link, a labeled navigation landmark, real in-page destinations, and a programmatically focusable main. Sprig wraps the navigation on small screens; it does not implement a hamburger menu or application routing. Keep ordinary site navigation as links, not ARIA menu widgets.
html:
Skip to main content
Community garden guide
  • Visiting
  • Access
  • Safety

Plan your garden visit

Use this guide to prepare for a shared outdoor space.

Visiting

Check the posted opening times at the entrance before entering.

Access

Keep paths clear and ask the on-site team about step-free routes.

Safety

Wear sturdy shoes and leave tools in their designated storage areas.
checks: Place the skip link as the first focusable element in the page, not inside another main or below an existing navigation bar.
Press Tab from the address bar: the skip link must become visible. Activate it and verify focus moves to main and subsequent Tab order starts after it.
Check all fragment destinations exist and the navigation landmark has a useful name; do not add role=button or role=menu to ordinary links.
Test wrapping at 320 CSS pixels, 400% zoom, and with longer translated link text; all links must remain visible and reachable.
When replacing fragments with real routes, use actual URLs and aria-current=page only on the active page link; do not hard-code a stale active state.

title: Email validation error connected with aria-describedby
description: An email form starts with a visible example error, a persistent label, aria-invalid, and hint/error IDs in aria-describedby. Explicit submit and input listeners use native validity properties to update the error and focus the invalid field. All checking is local; a valid email format is not proof that an address exists or that anything was saved.
html:
Check an email address

This local example starts with an invalid address. Nothing is sent or saved.

Enter an email address such as alex@example.org.

Include the part before @ and the email domain.
checks: Inspect the initial invalid state with a screen reader: label, required state, hint, and specific text error must be available without relying on red borders.
Submit an empty value and a malformed address; the visible error must match the problem, aria-invalid must be true, and focus must reach the email control.
Correct the address: hide the stale error, remove aria-invalid, and retain the hint association. Then invalidate and submit again to verify the error is restored.
Test keyboard submission and live status announcements in the target browser and screen reader, especially when the field already has focus.
The novalidate attribute is deliberate because this example supplies its own feedback using native validity properties. Keep submit disabled until its listener is attached.
For production, also validate on the server and test real failure paths; never treat a syntax check as successful delivery or persistence.

title: Scrollable data table with caption and scoped headers
description: A comparison table keeps native table semantics, a visible caption, scope=col and scope=row headers, and a labeled keyboard-focusable horizontal overflow region. The example minimum width makes narrow-screen scrolling deliberate rather than shrinking text. Do not replace data cells with a visual grid or add ARIA grid keyboard behavior.
html:
Compare meeting rooms

On narrow screens, focus the table region and use the arrow keys to scroll horizontally.

Example meeting rooms: capacity, equipment, and access
Room Seated capacity Equipment Step-free access Location
Willow 12 people Whiteboard Yes Ground floor, east entrance
Cedar 24 people Projector and whiteboard Yes, via lift First floor, beside the lift
Birch 8 people Whiteboard No; stairs only First floor, west staircase
checks: At a narrow viewport or high zoom, only the overflow region should scroll horizontally; the surrounding page must still reflow.
Tab to the labeled region, confirm a visible focus outline, and scroll both directions using the keyboard without a trap.
Use a screen reader's table navigation to confirm the caption and correct row and column headers are announced for data cells.
Retain native table, caption, th, and td elements; scope is suitable here because the header structure is simple and has no spans.
Check text contrast and full cell content in light, dark, and forced-colors modes; do not communicate access with color alone.

title: Empty state with a working local add-note action
description: A calm empty collection explains what to do next and provides a real Add a note button, labeled editor, save, cancel, and live feedback. Notes are held only in the current DOM and disappear on reload; there is no endpoint or persistence claim. This is an empty collection, not a loading spinner or a network-error placeholder.
html:
Session notes

Notes stay in this page only and disappear when you reload.

No notes yet

Add your first note to collect an idea for this session.

    Up to 500 characters. Saved only until this page is reloaded.
checks: Initially show only the empty message and available add action, not an empty list, a fake loading state, or an unexplained disabled control.
Activate Add a note with the keyboard and verify focus reaches its persistent label's textarea; cancel must discard the draft and restore focus.
Submit an empty note to check native required validation, then save real text: a list item must appear before the empty state is hidden.
Verify status announcements and focus restoration after saving. Add a second note to confirm the action remains usable.
Enter markup-like text and confirm it is rendered as text, not HTML. Reload to verify notes are not persisted, as disclosed.
For an empty search result instead, retain the search controls and offer a working clear-filters action; do not mislabel failures or loading as an empty collection.
